claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Nice to meet you! Thank you for letting me know about Alex.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask a couple more questions.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? (This would include things like A-levels, T-levels, or certain vocational qualifications, but not higher education like university.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually just left school recently. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

When Alex left school, did he register with the careers service (or Connexions) within 3 months of leaving education? And is he currently not in paid work of 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he registered pretty quickly after leaving school - definitely within the 3 months. And no, he's not working at all right now, just trying to figure out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It sounds like Alex is registered with the careers service and isn't currently working.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

Are you responsible for Alex, meaning he lives with you and you're the one looking after him and contributing to the cost of bringing him up?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives at home with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just one more question:

Do you live in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of the key reasons:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (he lives with you and you look after him)
- ✅ Alex is 16 years old
- ✅ Although Alex has left school, he registered with the careers service within 3 months of leaving education
- ✅ Alex is not in paid work of 24 hours or more per week

Under Child Benefit rules, you can continue to claim for a 16 or 17-year-old who has left education as long as they've registered with a qualifying organisation (like a careers service) and aren't working 24+ hours a week.

Please note that this eligibility will continue until Alex either turns 18, starts working 24 hours or more per week, or starts receiving certain benefits in his own right.

If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old. While he has left school, he registered with the local careers service within 3 months of leaving education, he is not in paid work of 24 hours or more per week, and he is under 18. Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or 17 who has left education or training if they register with a careers service, the armed forces, or a government-sponsored training organisation, and are not working 24 hours or more per week. Additionally, the claimant lives in the UK and is responsible for Alex (he lives with them and they are looking after him). All eligibility criteria are met.

The claimant therefore appears to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
